blocks.en: 📖 Deacon Family Ministry Plan — Unit 1: Biblical Foundations of the Diaconate
blocks.es_reference: 📖 Plan de Ministerio Familiar del Diácono — Unidad 1: Fundamentos Bíblicos del Diaconado

blocks.en: Professor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers
blocks.es_reference: Profesor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers

blocks.en: "For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His life a ransom for many." — Mark 10:45 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: «Porque el Hijo del Hombre no vino para ser servido, sino para servir, y para dar su vida en rescate por muchos.» — Marcos 10:45 (RVG)

blocks.en: Before a church can run a plan for its deacons, it must know what a deacon is. The Deacon Family Ministry Plan, which this course will study unit by unit, is a way of organizing the care of a whole congregation through its deacons; it was developed and is widely used among Southern Baptist churches. But a plan for deacons is only as good as its grasp of the office it serves. So in this first unit we set the plan aside and go back to the Scriptures to ask a simpler question: what kind of man, doing what kind of work, does the New Testament call a deacon?
blocks.es_reference: Antes de que una iglesia pueda llevar adelante un plan para sus diáconos, debe saber qué es un diácono. El Plan de Ministerio Familiar del Diácono, que este curso estudiará unidad por unidad, es una manera de organizar el cuidado de toda una congregación por medio de sus diáconos; fue desarrollado y se usa ampliamente entre las iglesias bautistas del Sur. Pero un plan para diáconos vale solo lo que vale su comprensión del oficio al que sirve. Así que en esta primera unidad dejamos el plan a un lado y volvemos a las Escrituras para hacer una pregunta más sencilla: ¿qué clase de hombre, haciendo qué clase de obra, llama diácono el Nuevo Testamento?

blocks.en: The answer begins with the word itself. "Deacon" is simply the English form of the Greek word diakonos, a common, humble word that means a servant — one who waits on tables, attends to needs, and serves others. The New Testament uses this word and its relatives (the verb diakoneō, to serve, and the noun diakonia, service or ministry) more than ninety times, very often of plain, ordinary service. By his very name, then, the deacon is a servant. He is not first a manager, a board member, or an officer of business. He is a servant of the church.
blocks.es_reference: La respuesta comienza con la palabra misma. «Diácono» es sencillamente la forma castellana de la palabra griega diakonos, una palabra común y humilde que significa siervo: el que sirve a las mesas, atiende necesidades y sirve a otros. El Nuevo Testamento usa esta palabra y sus derivados (el verbo diakoneō, servir, y el sustantivo diakonia, servicio o ministerio) más de noventa veces, muy a menudo de un servicio sencillo y ordinario. Por su mismo nombre, pues, el diácono es un siervo. No es primero un administrador, un miembro de junta ni un oficial de negocios. Es un siervo de la iglesia.

blocks.en: Far from lowering the man, the title honors him, for it is shared by the greatest. Paul calls himself a diakonos of the gospel and of the church (Ephesians 3:7; Colossians 1:25), and Scripture even calls Christ Himself a servant of the circumcision for the truth of God (Romans 15:8). The servant of the church follows the supreme Servant. Alongside Acts 6, two other passages anchor what the New Testament says about deacons: Philippians 1:1, where Paul greets the overseers and deacons as the two settled groups of leaders in a healthy church, and 1 Timothy 3:8–13, which lists the deacon's qualifications in detail. We will weigh those qualifications in Unit 2; here we lay the foundation beneath them all.
blocks.es_reference: Lejos de rebajar al hombre, el título lo honra, porque lo comparten los más grandes. Pablo se llama a sí mismo diakonos del evangelio y de la iglesia (Efesios 3:7; Colosenses 1:25), y la Escritura aun llama al mismo Cristo siervo de la circuncisión por la verdad de Dios (Romanos 15:8). El siervo de la iglesia sigue al Siervo supremo. Junto a Hechos 6, otros dos pasajes fundamentan lo que el Nuevo Testamento dice de los diáconos: Filipenses 1:1, donde Pablo saluda a los obispos y a los diáconos como los dos grupos establecidos de líderes en una iglesia sana, y 1 Timoteo 3:8–13, que enumera en detalle los requisitos del diácono. Sopesaremos esos requisitos en la Unidad 2; aquí ponemos el fundamento que está debajo de todos ellos.

blocks.en: This is exactly how the Lord Jesus defined greatness in His kingdom. Before any office called "deacon" existed, He had already overturned the world's order:
blocks.es_reference: Así definió exactamente el Señor Jesús la grandeza en su reino. Antes de que existiera oficio alguno llamado «diácono», Él ya había trastornado el orden del mundo:

blocks.en: Yet it shall not be so among you; but whoever desires to become great among you shall be your servant. And whoever of you desires to be first shall be slave of all. For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His life a ransom for many. (Mark 10:43–45, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: Mas no será así entre vosotros; sino que el que quiera hacerse grande entre vosotros será vuestro servidor, y el que de vosotros quiera ser el primero, será siervo de todos. Porque el Hijo del Hombre no vino para ser servido, sino para servir, y para dar su vida en rescate por muchos. (Marcos 10:43–45, RVG)

blocks.en: The office of deacon is this teaching made permanent — a standing, visible reminder in every church that its leaders serve the people; they do not lord over them. The deacon wears the towel, not the crown.
blocks.es_reference: El oficio del diácono es esta enseñanza hecha permanente: un recordatorio constante y visible en cada iglesia de que sus líderes sirven al pueblo; no se enseñorean de él. El diácono lleva la toalla, no la corona.

blocks.en: Illustration. In Mountains Beyond Mountains, Tracy Kidder tells of Dr. Paul Farmer, a Harvard physician who could have built a comfortable career anywhere he pleased. Instead, appalled by the suffering of the poor in Haiti, he poured out his life founding clinics that now serve about a million people. Challenged once that no one could love the children of strangers as his own, he answered, “All the great religions say, ‘love thy neighbor as thyself.’ I’m sorry. I can’t. But I’m going to keep on trying.” That is the servant’s heart the deacon is called to wear — a life spent for others rather than on itself.
blocks.es_reference: Ilustración. En Mountains Beyond Mountains, Tracy Kidder cuenta la historia del Dr. Paul Farmer, un médico de Harvard que pudo haber tenido una carrera cómoda donde quisiera. En cambio, consternado por el sufrimiento de los pobres en Haití, derramó su vida fundando clínicas que hoy atienden a cerca de un millón de personas. Cuando lo desafiaron diciendo que nadie podía amar a los hijos de extraños como a los propios, respondió: «Todas las grandes religiones dicen: “ama a tu prójimo como a ti mismo”. Lo siento. No puedo. Pero voy a seguir intentándolo». Ese es el corazón de siervo que el diácono está llamado a llevar — una vida gastada por los demás y no en sí misma.

blocks.en: Although the word "deacon" does not actually appear in the passage, the church has always seen the seed and pattern of the diaconate in the seven men chosen in Acts chapter 6. The fit is unmistakable: a practical need arises, spiritually qualified men are set apart to meet it, and the apostles are freed for the Word and prayer. From this one account we will draw five lessons about the ministry of the deacon.
blocks.es_reference: Aunque la palabra «diácono» no aparece de hecho en el pasaje, la iglesia siempre ha visto la semilla y el patrón del diaconado en los siete hombres escogidos en el capítulo 6 de Hechos. La correspondencia es inconfundible: surge una necesidad práctica, se apartan hombres espiritualmente calificados para atenderla, y los apóstoles quedan libres para la Palabra y la oración. De este solo relato sacaremos cinco lecciones sobre el ministerio del diácono.

blocks.en: Subject: the biblical origin and nature of the deacon's ministry.
blocks.es_reference: Tema: el origen y la naturaleza bíblicos del ministerio del diácono.

blocks.en: Proposition: God established the deacon's service so that practical care, entrusted to godly servants, would protect the ministry of the Word, guard the unity of the church, and advance the gospel.
blocks.es_reference: Proposición: Dios estableció el servicio del diácono para que el cuidado práctico, confiado a siervos piadosos, protegiera el ministerio de la Palabra, guardara la unidad de la iglesia y adelantara el evangelio.

blocks.en: I. The Need That Gave Rise to Servants
blocks.es_reference: I. La Necesidad que Dio Origen a los Siervos

blocks.en: The diaconate was not born out of theory but out of a very real, very awkward problem. The church in Jerusalem was growing quickly, and growth brought strain:
blocks.es_reference: El diaconado no nació de una teoría, sino de un problema muy real y muy incómodo. La iglesia en Jerusalén crecía rápidamente, y el crecimiento trajo tensión:

blocks.en: Now in those days, when the number of the disciples was multiplying, there arose a complaint against the Hebrews by the Hellenists, because their widows were neglected in the daily distribution. (Acts 6:1, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: En aquellos días, como creciera el número de los discípulos, hubo murmuración de los griegos contra los hebreos, de que las viudas de ellos eran desatendidas en el ministerio cotidiano. (Hechos 6:1, RVG)

blocks.en: The Greek-speaking (Hellenist) widows were being overlooked in the daily distribution of food, while the Hebrew widows were cared for. Notice what kind of problem this was. It was not a doctrinal heresy or an outside persecution; it was something as ordinary as hungry widows and the appearance of partiality at the food line. The first deacons were appointed to make sure that widows were fed and treated fairly. Here is the first lesson: deacon ministry begins where real human need meets the family of God. It is never beneath a deacon to attend to the practical, the physical, and the overlooked.
blocks.es_reference: Las viudas de habla griega (helenistas) eran pasadas por alto en la distribución diaria de los alimentos, mientras que las viudas hebreas sí recibían cuidado. Note qué clase de problema era este. No era una herejía doctrinal ni una persecución de afuera; era algo tan ordinario como viudas con hambre y la apariencia de favoritismo en el reparto. Los primeros diáconos fueron nombrados para asegurar que las viudas fueran alimentadas y tratadas con justicia. He aquí la primera lección: el ministerio del diácono comienza donde la verdadera necesidad humana se encuentra con la familia de Dios. Nunca es indigno de un diácono atender lo práctico, lo físico y lo olvidado.

blocks.en: Scripture never treats such care as a lesser thing. James makes it the very test of true religion: "Pure and undefiled religion before God and the Father is this: to visit orphans and widows in their trouble…" (James 1:27, NKJV). What the world counts small — a meal carried to a widow, a fair share at the table — heaven counts as worship. The deacon is the church's appointed hands for exactly this work.
blocks.es_reference: La Escritura nunca trata tal cuidado como cosa menor. Santiago lo hace la prueba misma de la religión verdadera: «La religión pura y sin mácula delante de Dios y Padre es esta: Visitar a los huérfanos y a las viudas en sus tribulaciones…» (Santiago 1:27, RVG). Lo que el mundo tiene por pequeño — una comida llevada a una viuda, una porción justa en la mesa — el cielo lo tiene por adoración. El diácono es las manos que la iglesia designa precisamente para esta obra.

blocks.en: Notice, too, the danger. A neglected need was breeding a complaint — a murmuring — that threatened the unity of the young church along ethnic lines. Practical neglect always carries spiritual consequences. Left unattended, the matter of the widows could have split the body in two. The deacon stands at exactly this point, where a quiet, unmet need could grow into a public wound.
blocks.es_reference: Note también el peligro. Una necesidad desatendida estaba engendrando una murmuración — una queja — que amenazaba la unidad de la joven iglesia por líneas étnicas. La negligencia práctica siempre lleva consecuencias espirituales. Sin atender, el asunto de las viudas pudo haber partido el cuerpo en dos. El diácono está precisamente en este punto, donde una necesidad callada y no atendida podría crecer hasta volverse una herida pública.

blocks.en: II. The Priority That Must Be Protected
blocks.es_reference: II. La Prioridad que Debe Protegerse

blocks.en: The apostles' response reveals the deacon's deepest purpose:
blocks.es_reference: La respuesta de los apóstoles revela el propósito más profundo del diácono:

blocks.en: Then the twelve summoned the multitude of the disciples and said, "It is not desirable that we should leave the word of God and serve tables." (Acts 6:2, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: Entonces los doce convocaron a la multitud de los discípulos, y dijeron: No es justo que nosotros dejemos la palabra de Dios, para servir a las mesas. (Hechos 6:2, RVG)

blocks.en: This is not contempt for serving tables. The apostles call the work good and worthy of seven Spirit-filled men; they simply recognize their own calling and its limits. If the Twelve tried to manage the food distribution personally, the ministry of the Word and prayer would suffer. So they resolved:
blocks.es_reference: Esto no es desprecio por servir a las mesas. Los apóstoles llaman a la obra buena y digna de siete hombres llenos del Espíritu; sencillamente reconocen su propio llamado y sus límites. Si los doce trataran de administrar personalmente el reparto de los alimentos, el ministerio de la Palabra y la oración sufriría. Por eso resolvieron:

blocks.en: but we will give ourselves continually to prayer and to the ministry of the word. (Acts 6:4, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: Y nosotros persistiremos en la oración, y en el ministerio de la palabra. (Hechos 6:4, RVG)

blocks.en: Here is the second lesson, and it is the heart of the office: the deacon exists to carry the load of practical care so that the spiritual leaders are freed for the Word and prayer. When the deacons serve well, the pastor can give himself to study, preaching, teaching, and prayer without being swallowed by tasks that others can do just as faithfully. The health of the pulpit is tied to the faithfulness of the deacons. A church served by devoted deacons is a church whose minister is free to feed it.
blocks.es_reference: He aquí la segunda lección, y es el corazón del oficio: el diácono existe para llevar la carga del cuidado práctico de modo que los líderes espirituales queden libres para la Palabra y la oración. Cuando los diáconos sirven bien, el pastor puede entregarse al estudio, a la predicación, a la enseñanza y a la oración sin ser absorbido por tareas que otros pueden hacer con igual fidelidad. La salud del púlpito está ligada a la fidelidad de los diáconos. Una iglesia servida por diáconos consagrados es una iglesia cuyo ministro queda libre para alimentarla.

blocks.en: This was the first division of labor in the Christian church, and it set a pattern for all time: good work must never be allowed to crowd out the best work. Every leader has limits of time and strength, and wisdom assigns each task to the right hands. The deacon, by taking up what would otherwise pull the minister away from the Word, guards the one ministry no one else can give the church.
blocks.es_reference: Esta fue la primera división del trabajo en la iglesia cristiana, y estableció un patrón para siempre: nunca se debe permitir que la obra buena desplace a la mejor obra. Todo líder tiene límites de tiempo y de fuerzas, y la sabiduría asigna cada tarea a las manos correctas. El diácono, al tomar lo que de otro modo apartaría al ministro de la Palabra, guarda el único ministerio que nadie más puede dar a la iglesia.

blocks.en: III. The Character That Must Be Required
blocks.es_reference: III. El Carácter que Debe Exigirse

blocks.en: When the apostles described the men to be chosen, their requirements are striking:
blocks.es_reference: Cuando los apóstoles describieron a los hombres que debían escogerse, sus requisitos son sorprendentes:

blocks.en: Therefore, brethren, seek out from among you seven men of good reputation, full of the Holy Spirit and wisdom, whom we may appoint over this business. (Acts 6:3, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: Buscad pues, hermanos, de entre vosotros a siete varones de buen testimonio, llenos del Espíritu Santo y de sabiduría, a quienes pongamos sobre este trabajo. (Hechos 6:3, RVG)

blocks.en: Three things are required, and not one of them is administrative skill. They must be of good reputation — men whose honesty is attested by the whole community. They must be full of the Holy Spirit — men whose lives are governed by God. And they must be full of wisdom — men of sound, practical judgment. The work was waiting on tables; the requirement was spiritual maturity. This is the third lesson: the church refused to separate practical service from spiritual character. A man who handles the church's people, money, and reputation must himself be a man of God. We will study these qualifications in detail in Unit 2, but already we see that a deacon is chosen for what he is before he is trusted with what he does.
blocks.es_reference: Se requieren tres cosas, y ninguna de ellas es habilidad administrativa. Deben ser de buen testimonio: hombres cuya honradez sea reconocida por toda la comunidad. Deben estar llenos del Espíritu Santo: hombres cuya vida es gobernada por Dios. Y deben estar llenos de sabiduría: hombres de juicio sano y práctico. La obra era servir a las mesas; el requisito era madurez espiritual. Esta es la tercera lección: la iglesia se negó a separar el servicio práctico del carácter espiritual. Un hombre que maneja a la gente, el dinero y la reputación de la iglesia debe ser él mismo un hombre de Dios. Estudiaremos estos requisitos en detalle en la Unidad 2, pero ya vemos que un diácono es escogido por lo que es antes de que se le confíe lo que hace.

blocks.en: Notice the pairing of the two inward marks. To be full of the Holy Spirit is to be governed Godward — yielded, holy, and led by God; to be full of wisdom is to be capable manward — sound and discerning in the affairs of people. The church wanted both, for a man may be devout yet imprudent, or shrewd yet unspiritual, and neither alone is fit to serve. Together they describe a mature believer the congregation can trust with its weakest members and its most delicate needs.
blocks.es_reference: Note el par de las dos marcas interiores. Estar lleno del Espíritu Santo es ser gobernado hacia Dios — rendido, santo y guiado por Dios; estar lleno de sabiduría es ser capaz hacia los hombres — sensato y de buen discernimiento en los asuntos de la gente. La iglesia quería ambas, porque un hombre puede ser devoto pero imprudente, o astuto pero carnal, y ninguna de las dos basta por sí sola. Juntas describen a un creyente maduro a quien la congregación puede confiar sus miembros más débiles y sus necesidades más delicadas.

blocks.en: IV. The Church That Sets Them Apart
blocks.es_reference: IV. La Iglesia que los Aparta

blocks.en: The manner of their appointment is as instructive as the men themselves:
blocks.es_reference: La manera de su nombramiento es tan instructiva como los hombres mismos:

blocks.en: …whom they set before the apostles; and when they had prayed, they laid hands on them. (Acts 6:6, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: …a los cuales presentaron ante los apóstoles, quienes, orando, les impusieron las manos. (Hechos 6:6, RVG)

blocks.en: The whole congregation chose the seven — and Stephen is named first among them. They then presented these men to the apostles, who confirmed and commissioned them with prayer and the laying on of hands. See the beautiful partnership: the body chooses, and the leaders confirm. Deacon ministry is neither self-appointed nor autocratically imposed; it rises from the church and is set apart before God. The laying on of hands was not a magic rite but a public recognition and blessing, marking these men out for holy service. This is the fourth lesson, and it tells us where a deacon's authority comes from: it is not seized but conferred by the church and consecrated in prayer.
blocks.es_reference: Toda la congregación escogió a los siete — y Esteban es nombrado primero entre ellos —. Luego presentaron a estos hombres a los apóstoles, quienes los confirmaron y comisionaron con oración e imposición de manos. Vea la hermosa colaboración: el cuerpo escoge, y los líderes confirman. El ministerio del diácono no es autonombrado ni impuesto de manera autocrática; surge de la iglesia y es apartado delante de Dios. La imposición de manos no era un rito mágico, sino un reconocimiento y una bendición públicos, que señalaban a estos hombres para un servicio santo. Esta es la cuarta lección, y nos dice de dónde viene la autoridad de un diácono: no se toma, sino que la confiere la iglesia y se consagra en oración.

blocks.en: V. The Fruit That Service Bears
blocks.es_reference: V. El Fruto que Produce el Servicio

blocks.en: The chapter ends not with full stomachs but with an explosion of the gospel:
blocks.es_reference: El capítulo no termina con estómagos llenos, sino con una explosión del evangelio:

blocks.en: Then the word of God spread, and the number of the disciples multiplied greatly in Jerusalem, and a great many of the priests were obedient to the faith. (Acts 6:7, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: Y crecía la palabra del Señor, y el número de los discípulos se multiplicaba grandemente en Jerusalén; también una gran multitud de los sacerdotes obedecía a la fe. (Hechos 6:7, RVG)

blocks.en: This is no accident of arrangement. With the widows cared for, the unity of the church restored, and the apostles freed to preach, the Word of God ran and the church grew — so much that even many of the priests came to faith. Here is the fifth lesson: servant ministry and gospel growth are tied together. When deacons take up the burden of care so that the Word can be preached and the body kept in peace, God blesses His church with increase. The deacon's quiet, practical service is the soil in which the preached Word bears fruit.
blocks.es_reference: Esto no es una casualidad de arreglo. Con las viudas atendidas, la unidad de la iglesia restaurada y los apóstoles libres para predicar, la Palabra de Dios corrió y la iglesia creció — tanto que aun muchos de los sacerdotes vinieron a la fe —. He aquí la quinta lección: el ministerio de servicio y el crecimiento del evangelio están unidos. Cuando los diáconos toman la carga del cuidado para que la Palabra pueda predicarse y el cuerpo se mantenga en paz, Dios bendice a su iglesia con aumento. El servicio callado y práctico del diácono es la tierra en que la Palabra predicada da fruto.

blocks.en: Conclusion
blocks.es_reference: Conclusión

blocks.en: Gather the five lessons and you have the heart of the office. The deacon's very name means servant. His Lord defined greatness as service and washed feet to prove it. His pattern in Acts 6 shows a service that meets real need, protects the Word, requires godly character, rises from the church, and bears gospel fruit. The deacon is, in a word, service made holy.
blocks.es_reference: Reúna las cinco lecciones y tendrá el corazón del oficio. El mismo nombre del diácono significa siervo. Su Señor definió la grandeza como servicio y lavó los pies para probarlo. Su patrón en Hechos 6 muestra un servicio que atiende la necesidad real, protege la Palabra, exige carácter piadoso, surge de la iglesia y produce fruto del evangelio. El diácono es, en una palabra, el servicio hecho santo.

blocks.en: Every Christian is called to this servant spirit, but the deacon is called to embody it before the whole church, so that when the congregation looks at him it sees a living picture of the Lord who came not to be served but to serve. That is a high calling clothed in humble work. It is a calling that costs a man his comfort and his pride, yet it repays him with the quiet dignity of standing where his Master once stood — towel in hand, among the very people he loves. The church has never lacked for men willing to lead; its deepest need, in every generation, is for men willing to serve.
blocks.es_reference: Todo cristiano es llamado a este espíritu de siervo, pero el diácono es llamado a encarnarlo delante de toda la iglesia, de modo que cuando la congregación lo mira, ve un retrato vivo del Señor que vino no para ser servido, sino para servir. Ese es un llamado alto vestido de obra humilde. Es un llamado que le cuesta al hombre su comodidad y su orgullo, pero que le recompensa con la dignidad serena de estar donde su Señor estuvo — con la toalla en la mano, entre las mismas personas que ama. A la iglesia nunca le han faltado hombres dispuestos a dirigir; su necesidad más profunda, en cada generación, es de hombres dispuestos a servir.

blocks.en: Illustration. Ralph Neighbour tells of a man named Jack, a corporation president who was ruthlessly cast aside when he was diagnosed with cancer, burning through his insurance and his savings with a wife and daughter to leave behind. A deacon and his pastor came to visit. At first the deacon offended him, asking whether he had prepared for life after death, and Jack ordered them out. But the deacon went back, humbly apologized, and then told him this: a realtor in the church would sell Jack’s house and donate the commission; the men of the church would make the payments until it sold; an apartment owner had offered his widow a home, free utilities, and a salary; and the proceeds would send his daughter to college. “Jack cried like a baby.” He died still resisting Christ — yet he had felt the love of God through a deacon’s hands, and his widow, moved by that care, later came to faith. That is the Deacon Family Ministry Plan at work before it ever had a name.
blocks.es_reference: Ilustración. Ralph Neighbour cuenta la historia de un hombre llamado Jack, un presidente de empresa al que descartaron sin piedad cuando le diagnosticaron cáncer, y que agotó su seguro y sus ahorros, dejando una esposa y una hija. Un diácono y su pastor fueron a visitarlo. Al principio el diácono lo ofendió al preguntarle si se había preparado para la vida después de la muerte, y Jack los echó. Pero el diácono volvió, se disculpó humildemente, y luego le dijo esto: un agente de bienes raíces de la iglesia vendería su casa y donaría su comisión; los hombres de la iglesia harían los pagos hasta venderla; un dueño de apartamentos había ofrecido a su viuda un hogar, servicios gratuitos y un salario; y lo recaudado pagaría los estudios de su hija. «Jack lloró como un niño». Murió resistiendo todavía a Cristo — pero había sentido el amor de Dios por las manos de un diácono, y su viuda, conmovida por ese cuidado, más tarde vino a la fe. Eso es el Plan de Ministerio Familiar del Diácono obrando antes de tener nombre.

blocks.en: The Deacon Family Ministry Plan, which we take up beginning in Unit 4, is simply one careful, proven way to put Acts 6 into practice in a local church: to make sure that in a growing congregation no "widow" is neglected, every family is known and cared for, and the pastor is freed for the Word. Before we ever learn the plan, we must have the heart, for if we forget the heart the plan becomes mere machinery, but if we keep the heart the plan becomes living service. The deacon is a servant — and his service is the ground in which the Word of God grows.
blocks.es_reference: El Plan de Ministerio Familiar del Diácono, que tomaremos a partir de la Unidad 4, es sencillamente una manera cuidadosa y probada de poner Hechos 6 en práctica en una iglesia local: asegurar que en una congregación que crece ninguna «viuda» sea desatendida, que cada familia sea conocida y cuidada, y que el pastor quede libre para la Palabra. Antes de aprender el plan, debemos tener el corazón, porque si olvidamos el corazón el plan se vuelve pura maquinaria, pero si guardamos el corazón el plan se vuelve servicio vivo. El diácono es un siervo, y su servicio es la tierra en que crece la Palabra de Dios.

mc.stem: The word "deacon" comes from the Greek word diakonos, which simply means:
mc.why: Diakonos is a common, humble word meaning servant.

mc.stem: In Mark 10:43–45, Jesus taught that whoever desires to be great among you shall be:
mc.why: Jesus defined greatness as service: the great one must be the servant (Mark 10:43).

mc.stem: Although the word "deacon" is not used there, the church has long seen the seed of the diaconate in:
mc.why: The seven men chosen in Acts 6 are seen as the prototype of the diaconate.

mc.stem: What practical problem in Acts 6 gave rise to the choosing of the seven?
options: There was no money in the treasury
The Greek-speaking widows were neglected in the daily distribution
mc.why: The Hellenist widows were being neglected in the daily distribution of food (Acts 6:1).

mc.stem: The neglected widows were creating what danger in the young church?
options: a complaint that threatened the church's unity
mc.why: A complaint (murmuring) arose that threatened the unity of the church (Acts 6:1).

mc.stem: The apostles said it was not desirable that they should leave _____ to serve tables.
mc.why: "It is not desirable that we should leave the word of God and serve tables" (Acts 6:2).

mc.stem: Which best describes the apostles' attitude toward serving tables?
options: They recognized it as good work, but not their primary calling
They despised it as beneath them
They refused to let anyone else do it
mc.why: They called it good work worthy of Spirit-filled men, but recognized their own calling to the Word and prayer.

mc.stem: The deepest purpose of the deacon, drawn from Acts 6, is to:
options: govern the church as a board
carry practical care so leaders are freed for the Word and prayer
mc.why: The deacon carries the practical load so the spiritual leaders can give themselves to the Word and prayer (Acts 6:2-4).

mc.stem: What three qualifications did the apostles require of the seven?
options: good reputation, the Holy Spirit, and wisdom
mc.why: Men of good reputation, full of the Holy Spirit and wisdom (Acts 6:3).

mc.stem: Notably, the list of qualifications for the seven did NOT include:
options: being full of the Holy Spirit
mc.why: Not one of the three requirements is administrative skill; all are spiritual.

mc.stem: Who chose the seven men?
mc.why: The whole multitude (congregation) chose the seven (Acts 6:5).

mc.stem: After the seven were chosen, what did the apostles do?
options: prayed and laid hands on them
mc.why: They set them before the apostles, who prayed and laid hands on them (Acts 6:6).

mc.stem: The first deacon named in the list of the seven was:
mc.why: Stephen is named first among the seven (Acts 6:5).

mc.stem: The laying on of hands signified:
options: public recognition and the church's blessing
mc.why: It was a public recognition and blessing, setting the men apart for service.

mc.stem: According to Acts 6:7, what happened after the matter of the widows was resolved?
options: the word of God spread and the disciples multiplied greatly
mc.why: The word of God spread and the number of disciples multiplied greatly (Acts 6:7).

mc.stem: Acts 6:7 also notes that a great many of whom became obedient to the faith?
mc.why: A great many of the priests were obedient to the faith (Acts 6:7).

mc.stem: The relationship Acts 6 shows between practical service and gospel growth is that they are:
options: tied together — servant ministry freed the Word to spread
mc.why: With the apostles freed to preach, the Word spread; service and gospel growth are tied together.

mc.stem: A deacon's authority, according to the Acts 6 pattern, is best described as:
options: conferred by the church and consecrated before God
mc.why: It is not seized but conferred by the church and consecrated in prayer.

mc.stem: "Deacon ministry begins where real human need meets the family of God." This means a deacon should:
options: not consider practical or physical care beneath him
mc.why: It is never beneath a deacon to attend to the practical, physical, and overlooked.

mc.stem: The Deacon Family Ministry Plan, studied in this course, is best understood as:
options: one proven way to put the Acts 6 pattern of servant care into practice
a business model for rapid church growth

fill.prompt: "Deacon" is simply the English form of the Greek word ____, a humble word that means a servant.
In Philippians 1:1 Paul greets the ____ and deacons as the two settled groups of leaders in a healthy church.
In Acts 6:1 a complaint arose against the Hebrews by the Hellenists, because their ____ were neglected in the daily distribution.
The Twelve said, "It is not desirable that we should leave the word of God and serve ____" (Acts 6:2).
The apostles resolved, "We will give ourselves continually to ____ and to the ministry of the word" (Acts 6:4).
The church was told to seek out seven men of good ____, full of the Holy Spirit and wisdom (Acts 6:3).
To be full of ____ is to be capable manward, sound and discerning in the affairs of people.

sa.prompt: What does the word "deacon" mean, and how did Jesus define greatness in Mark 10:43–45?
sa.model: The word "deacon" comes from the Greek diakonos, which simply means a servant or one who waits on others. In Mark 10:43-45 Jesus turned the world's idea of greatness upside down, teaching that whoever wants to be great must be a servant, and whoever wants to be first must be slave of all, for even the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve and to give His life a ransom for many. So the deacon's very name and his Lord's own example both define his work as humble service to others.

sa.prompt: Describe the practical problem in Acts 6 that led to the choosing of the seven.
sa.model: As the church multiplied, the Greek-speaking (Hellenist) widows were being neglected in the daily distribution of food, while the Hebrew widows were cared for. This neglect produced a complaint that threatened the unity of the young church. The need was very ordinary, making sure widows were fed and treated without partiality, yet it carried real spiritual danger. It was to meet this practical need that the apostles called for seven qualified servants.

sa.prompt: Why did the apostles refuse to leave the Word of God to serve tables, and what does this teach about the deacon's purpose?
sa.model: The apostles did not despise serving tables; they called it good work worthy of Spirit-filled men. Rather, they recognized their own calling and limits: they could not give themselves fully to the ministry of the word and to prayer if they were also managing the daily distribution. This teaches the deacon's deepest purpose, to carry the load of practical care so that the spiritual leaders are freed for the Word and prayer. When deacons serve well, the pastor can preach and pray, and the whole church is fed.

sa.prompt: What three qualifications did the apostles require of the seven, and what is striking about the list?
sa.model: The apostles told the church to choose seven men of good reputation, full of the Holy Spirit, and full of wisdom. What is striking is that not one of these three is administrative skill or business ability. The work was serving tables, but the requirement was spiritual maturity and proven character. The church refused to separate practical service from godliness, because a man who handles the church's people, money, and reputation must himself be a man of God.

sa.prompt: Who chose the seven, who set them apart, and what did the laying on of hands signify?
sa.model: The whole congregation chose the seven men, and Stephen is named first. They set these men before the apostles, who prayed and laid hands on them. This shows a beautiful partnership: the body chooses, and the leaders confirm and commission. The laying on of hands was not magic; it was public recognition and the church's blessing, setting the men apart for their service before God. A deacon's authority is therefore not seized but conferred by the church and consecrated in prayer.

sa.prompt: According to Acts 6:7, what was the fruit of resolving the matter of the widows? What does this teach about service and gospel growth?
sa.model: Acts 6:7 says that after the matter was resolved, the word of God spread, the number of the disciples multiplied greatly, and a great many of the priests became obedient to the faith. The fruit of organizing practical care was not merely full stomachs but an explosion of the Word. With the apostles freed to preach and the church's unity restored, the gospel ran. This teaches that servant ministry and gospel growth are tied together: when deacons carry the burden of care, the Word is preached and the church grows.

sa.prompt: Explain why a deacon should never consider practical or physical care "beneath him."
sa.model: Deacon ministry begins where real human need meets the family of God. The first deacons were appointed to make sure widows were fed and treated fairly, a very ordinary, practical task. Because the deacon's very name means servant, and because his Lord washed feet and served, no act of humble care is beneath him. When a deacon attends to the physical and the overlooked, a meal, a visit, a need quietly met, he is doing the very work the office was created for, and he honors Christ in it.

sa.prompt: How does the deacon's office protect the ministry of the Word?
sa.model: The deacon's office protects the ministry of the Word by carrying the practical burdens that would otherwise consume the pastor's time and strength. In Acts 6 the apostles could not manage the daily distribution and still give themselves fully to the word and prayer, so the church set servants over the practical work. When deacons faithfully handle care, finances, and the needs of families, the pastor is freed to study, preach, teach, and pray. In this way the faithfulness of the deacons is tied to the health of the pulpit.

sa.prompt: Summarize the partnership between the congregation and the leaders in appointing deacons (Acts 6:5-6).
sa.model: Acts 6 shows a balanced partnership. The whole congregation was invited to select seven qualified men from among themselves, and they did so, choosing Stephen and the others. Then they presented these men to the apostles, who confirmed them by prayer and the laying on of hands. So deacon ministry is neither self-appointed nor autocratically imposed: it rises from the body and is set apart by the leaders. The people recognize the gifts; the leaders commission and bless. This guards both the congregation's voice and the church's order.

sa.prompt: In your own words, why is understanding the office of deacon necessary before learning the Deacon Family Ministry Plan?
sa.model: A plan for deacons is only as good as its grasp of what a deacon is. Before we can organize families and assignments, we must see that the deacon is at heart a servant, defined by his name, by his Lord who came to serve, and by the Acts 6 pattern of practical care that protects the Word and guards unity. The Deacon Family Ministry Plan is simply one proven way to put that biblical pattern into practice, making sure that in a growing church no family is neglected and the pastor is freed for the Word. If we forget the heart, the plan becomes mere machinery; if we keep the heart, the plan becomes living service.
